source_species_detail: Human OSM receptor comparison in JAR and A375 cells; receptor cloning and signaling assays
citation_note: Signaling of type II OSM receptor; dual OSM receptors
evidence_summary: Both LIFR-gp130 and OSMR-gp130 receptor complexes activate JAK-family kinases and STAT3; STAT5b was specific to the type-II OSMR-gp130 complex.
limitations: No SCI receiver-cell context; receptor-specific branch weights are not quantified.

source_species_detail: Human IFN receptor biochemical systems and JAK1-deficient cell line
citation_note: Type-I interferon receptor/JAK/STAT reconstitution and STAT2 loss-of-function
evidence_summary: IFNAR1-TYK2 and IFNAR2-JAK1 associations, type-I IFN activation of STAT1/STAT2, and STAT2-dependent ISGF3 formation are supported; JAK1 complementation restores IFN response.
limitations: Most evidence is biochemical or transformed-cell comparator evidence.

source_species_detail: Human receptor-component cell systems, IFNGR2-deficient mouse cells, and fibroblast signaling assays
citation_note: IFN-gamma receptor complex and Pyk2 branch
evidence_summary: IFNGR1/2 activates JAK1, JAK2, and STAT1; IFNGR2 loss blocks signaling; Pyk2 supports IFN-gamma-specific ERK/STAT1 branch behavior.
limitations: Pyk2/ERK is branch-specific and should not be exported as a universal IFN relay.

source_species_detail: Mammalian TNFR1 signaling complexes and TNF-induced death-branch assays
citation_note: TNFR1 TRADD/TRAF2/FADD bifurcation and RIPK1 death-complex study
evidence_summary: TRADD links TNFR1 to TRAF2 and FADD; TRAF2 and FADD separate NF-kappaB and apoptotic branches, while RIPK1 remains relevant to necrotic/death outputs.
limitations: Does not resolve all cell-state-specific TNF MAPK and necroptosis edges.

source_species_detail: IL-1 receptor signaling and MyD88 isoform/IRAK experiments in mammalian cells
citation_note: IL-1 MyD88 IRAK TRAF6 NF-kappaB/JNK relay
evidence_summary: MyD88 and IRAK are required for IL-1 responses; IRAK supports TRAF6/TAB2 recruitment; the MyD88 short isoform fails to recruit IRAK4.
limitations: Some papers resolve IRAK as a combined node; exact IRAK4-to-IRAK1 ordering is retained conservatively.

source_species_detail: CXCR4-expressing mammalian cell systems, live-cell imaging, migration assays, and pertussis-toxin/knockdown studies
citation_note: CXCL12/CXCR4 G-protein, Akt/ERK, and Src-EGFR cross-talk
evidence_summary: CXCR4 signaling activates Akt and ERK, depends on G-protein-linked signaling, and can use Src-mediated EGFR transactivation in a context-dependent branch.
limitations: Chemokine receptor subtypes and ligand-biased signaling are not saturated here.

source_species_detail: Mammalian epithelial systems and biochemical Smad signaling analyses
citation_note: TGF-beta receptor-mediated Smad2/3/4 signaling
evidence_summary: TGF-beta receptor phosphorylation of Smad2/3 and R-Smad/Smad4 nuclear relay are supported.
limitations: Noncanonical TGF-beta branches are not yet saturated.

source_species_detail: Early mouse embryo and BMP receptor/R-Smad signaling systems
citation_note: BMP dose-dependent Smad1/5/8 signaling
evidence_summary: BMP receptors activate Smad1/5/8, which are retained as a cooperative R-Smad branch with Smad4.
limitations: Paralog-specific use and adult SCI cell context remain open.

source_species_detail: EGFR-expressing mammalian cells and PC12 signaling comparisons
citation_note: EGFR Shc-Grb2-Sos-Ras and parallel PI3K-AKT/ERK branches
evidence_summary: EGF induces receptor/Shc/Grb2/Sos coupling, Ras-GEF activity, and ERK signaling; EGFR also supports a parallel PI3K-AKT branch.
limitations: The register intentionally does not force a single adaptor or encode signal duration.

source_species_detail: FGFR-expressing fibroblasts and FRS2 biochemical studies
citation_note: FGFR-FRS2 positive and negative branch evidence
evidence_summary: FRS2A deficiency impairs FGF-induced ERK and PI3K activation; FRS2-bound Grb2/Sos and PI3K are retained, with Cbl as an attenuation boundary.
limitations: FGFR paralog and ligand-specific differences are not resolved.

source_species_detail: NIH-3T3 fibroblasts stimulated with PDGF
citation_note: PDGF receptor association with PI3K
evidence_summary: PDGF stimulation produces rapid PDGFR-PI3K association and PI3K activity.
limitations: Downstream AKT and ERK links are not separately source-resolved in this packet.

source_species_detail: Primary human lymphatic endothelial cells and endothelial signaling systems
citation_note: VEGFR2-PLC/ERK and VEGFR2-PI3K/AKT branch evidence
evidence_summary: VEGFR2-specific inhibition separates PLC/ERK and PI3K/AKT branches; VEGFR3 also directly interacts with PI3K in lymphatic endothelial cells.
limitations: This is vascular-endothelial comparator evidence, not SCI astrocyte evidence.

source_species_detail: Vertebrate and mammalian WNT signalosome, knockdown, and phosphorylation assays
citation_note: WNT FZD-LRP6-DVL signalosome and beta-catenin output
evidence_summary: WNT induces FZD/LRP6/DVL signalosome formation, LRP6 phosphorylation, Axin/GSK3 recruitment, and beta-catenin pathway activation.
limitations: Noncanonical WNT/JNK and PCP branches are not yet saturated.

source_species_detail: Mammalian Notch processing, NICD-CSL/RBPJ interaction, reporter, and target-gene assays
citation_note: Notch proteolysis to NICD/RBPJ and HES/HEY output
evidence_summary: Gamma-secretase-dependent NICD release, NICD-RBPJ/CSL complex formation, and HES1/HEY1 transcriptional regulation are supported.
limitations: Ligand-specific receptor paralog differences and noncanonical Notch outputs remain open.

source_species_detail: Human cytokine/receptor constructs in murine Ba/F3 cells reconstituted with CNTFRa-gp130-LIFR or CNTFRa-gp130-OSMR
citation_note: CNTFR-specific LIFR and OSMR complex signaling
evidence_summary: CNTF stimulated STAT3 phosphorylation and cell proliferation through both CNTFRa-gp130-LIFR and alternative CNTFRa-gp130-OSMR complexes.
limitations: Reconstituted Ba/F3 systems establish receptor-complex competence but do not establish injured-SCI astrocyte branch weights.

source_species_detail: Mature murine cortical astrocytes and ROS17/2.8 astrocyte-like cells treated with CNTF, soluble CNTFRa, AG490, and dye-transfer assays
citation_note: CNTF-CNTFRa-JAK-STAT3 to Cx43 and coupling
evidence_summary: CNTF-CNTFRa treatment induced Cx43 expression and intercellular coupling with nuclear phospho-STAT3; AG490 blocked the functional output.
limitations: Astrocyte culture and soluble-receptor context; receptor subunit stoichiometry is not resolved in injured spinal cord.

source_species_detail: Primary spinal cord astrocytes, astrocyte-neuron cocultures, direct spinal CNTF injection, and rat spinal contusion tissue
citation_note: CNTF astrocyte activation and neurotrophic support
evidence_summary: CNTF activated spinal astrocytes, increased FGF2 production/release and neuronal support, and was accompanied by increased CNTF/pSTAT3-related signals after spinal contusion.
limitations: Functional SCI/CNS evidence does not isolate CNTFRa-gp130-LIFR versus CNTFRa-gp130-OSMR usage or prove a direct CNTF-to-STAT3 edge in the injured astrocyte state.

source_species_detail: Human U2OS cells expressing synthetic type-III interferon receptor pairs with TYK2-deficient comparison
citation_note: Type-III interferon receptor-associated kinase requirement
evidence_summary: Type-III receptor reconstitution and TYK2 perturbation support JAK/TYK2 participation in IFN-lambda-induced STAT activation.
limitations: Synthetic receptor context; do not transfer type-III receptor findings to IFNAR/IFNGR or assume the same branch in astrocytes.

source_species_detail: Primary human astrocytes treated with IFN-lambda, receptor-blocking antibodies, poly-I:C, and HSV-1 infection
citation_note: IFN-lambda astrocyte IRF/ISG and antiviral output
evidence_summary: IFN-lambda induced IRF/ISG programs and reduced HSV-1 replication in primary human astrocytes; receptor blockade attenuated the antiviral effect.
limitations: The papers support a pathway/function layer but do not isolate a necessary JAK/STAT kinase step in astrocytes.

source_species_detail: Human TNFR2 and reporter systems with TRAF2 overexpression or dominant-negative TRAF2
citation_note: TNFR2-TRAF2 adaptor recruitment and NF-kappaB
evidence_summary: TRAF2 was sufficient for and dominant-negative TRAF2 inhibited TNFR2-mediated NF-kappaB activation, supporting TRAF2 as a proximal TNFR2 relay adaptor.
limitations: Overexpression/reporter context; does not define all endogenous TNFR2 adaptor usage.

source_species_detail: TNFR2 mutant/reporter systems, tumor cell lines, and primary T-cell signaling assays
citation_note: TNFR2 canonical and alternative NF-kappaB branches
evidence_summary: TNFR2 recruits TRAF2 and activates NF-kappaB/JNK; membrane TNF-TNFR2 selectively supports alternative NF-kappaB/p100 processing in the cited systems.
limitations: Ligand form, receptor abundance, and cell state alter branch strength; no SCI astrocyte-specific molecular perturbation is established.

source_species_detail: Adult mouse cuprizone-demyelinated corpus callosum, activated astrocytes, TNFR2-deficient mice, and CXCL12 lentiviral rescue
citation_note: TNFR2 astrocyte-CXCL12-OPC repair relay
evidence_summary: TNFR2 activity in activated astrocytes was required for CXCL12 upregulation and downstream OPC proliferation/differentiation during remyelination.
limitations: CNS demyelination comparator, not traumatic SCI; the paper does not isolate the biochemical TRAF2/NF-kappaB step in astrocytes.

source_species_detail: Rat contusive SCI treated with a TNFR2-specific agonist and mouse TNFR1/TNFR2 deletion after SCI
citation_note: TNFR2 functional SCI protection and recovery boundary
evidence_summary: TNFR2 agonism improved locomotor recovery in rat contusion, while receptor deletion studies support TNFR-NF-kappaB/c-IAP2 survival context after SCI.
limitations: Functional evidence does not identify a single receiver cell or prove TNFR2-specific intracellular causality in astrocytes.

source_species_detail: Human B cells and murine EL-4-derived receptor systems with IL1R2/IL1RAP chimeric and crosslinking assays
citation_note: IL1R2 decoy complex and IL1RAP sequestration
evidence_summary: Ligated IL1R2 interacted with IL1RAP but lacked a signaling TIR domain, supporting dominant-negative interference with IL1R1-IL1RAP assembly.
limitations: Chimeric receptor and crosslinking evidence establishes decoy-complex behavior, not an intracellular IL1R2 relay.

source_species_detail: Human HEK293, COS, and OVCAR-3 cells expressing IL1R1 or IL1R2
citation_note: IL1R2 selective shedding and soluble decoy function
evidence_summary: Only IL1R2, not IL1R1, underwent rapid phorbol-induced shedding, consistent with soluble decoy regulation of IL-1 responsiveness.
limitations: The study measures receptor release and decoy behavior rather than an astrocyte or SCI response.

source_species_detail: Primary mouse astrocytes and conditional IL1R1 restoration/deletion in spinal cord injury models
citation_note: Astrocyte IL1R1-ROS-oligodendrocyte loss branch
evidence_summary: Astrocyte IL1R1 was required for IL-1alpha-induced ROS and downstream oligodendrocyte loss after central administration and SCI-associated injury paradigms.
limitations: This is IL1R1 signaling evidence and does not establish IL1R2 expression or decoy action in SCI astrocytes.

source_species_detail: Human CCR4, CCR7, and CCR10 receptor assays using G-protein and beta-arrestin BRET readouts
citation_note: CCL/CCR receptor-specific G-protein and arrestin branch comparison
evidence_summary: CCL17/CCL22 at CCR4 favored beta-arrestin recruitment, while CCL19/CCL21 at CCR7 activated both G-protein and beta-arrestin responses in a matched cellular background.
limitations: Engineered receptor assays do not establish branch weights in SCI receiver cells.

source_species_detail: Human CXCR3A and CXCR3B splice-variant signaling assays with ligand stimulation, beta-arrestin recruitment, ERK, and G-protein readouts
citation_note: CXCR3 splice-variant branch distinction
evidence_summary: CXCL9/10/11 produced distinct G-protein, beta-arrestin, and ERK outputs across CXCR3A versus CXCR3B.
limitations: Splice-variant comparison is not equivalent to a universal ligand bias map or SCI glial evidence.

source_species_detail: RIBL17 mink lung epithelial cells and AML12 mouse hepatocyte signaling systems with receptor mutants, TRAF6 mutants, RNAi, and kinase assays
citation_note: TGFBR-TRAF6-TAK1-JNK/p38 noncanonical relay
evidence_summary: TGF-beta receptor complexes interacted with TRAF6, induced K63 ubiquitination and TRAF6-TAK1 association, and required this module for JNK/p38 activation.
limitations: Pathway-complex resolution is retained; exact receptor compartment and cell-type dependence remain context-specific.

source_species_detail: Developing mouse retinal ganglion cells with BMPR2 receptor-tail mutants and axon-growth assays
citation_note: BMPR2-LIMK1 noncanonical cytoskeletal branch
evidence_summary: BMPR2 receptor-tail interaction with LIMK1 was required for BMP-dependent retinal axon extension.
limitations: Developmental neural context; not SCI astrocyte evidence.

source_species_detail: Adult rat demyelinating spinal cord lesions and cultured mature spinal cord astrocytes treated with BMP4/BMP7 and noggin
citation_note: BMP-SMAD1/5/8 astrocyte branch and CSPG output
evidence_summary: BMP4/BMP7 increased astrocyte pSMAD1/5/8, nuclear SMAD1, GFAP, aggrecan, and neurocan; noggin blocked the CSPG response.
limitations: Demyelinating lesion rather than contusion SCI; downstream CSPG output is functional evidence.

source_species_detail: Mouse cortical injury, fibrinogen-bound latent TGF-beta, primary astrocytes, and TGFBR inhibition
citation_note: TGF-beta-Smad2 astrocyte scar branch
evidence_summary: TGF-beta receptor inhibition reduced Smad2 phosphorylation, astrocyte activation, and neurocan deposition after vascular/CNS injury.
limitations: Cortical injury rather than spinal cord injury; no noncanonical TGF-beta branch is claimed by this edge.

source_species_detail: NIH3T3 fibroblasts, mouse vascular smooth-muscle cells, PDGFR mutants, Src/PI3K/PKC perturbations, and ERK assays
citation_note: PDGFR-Src and PDGFR-ERK branches
evidence_summary: PDGFR signaling activated Src and ERK through receptor-associated PI3K/PKC/redox and adaptor-dependent mechanisms.
limitations: Exact adaptor ordering and cell-type-specific branch balance remain unresolved.

source_species_detail: CNS oligodendrocyte progenitor cultures and developing CNS migration assays with ERK inhibitors
citation_note: PDGF-A-ERK oligodendrocyte progenitor migration
evidence_summary: PDGF-A induced OPC migration and a self-sustaining ERK signal that persisted after the initiating stimulus.
limitations: Neural progenitor comparator; does not isolate a single PDGFR paralog in the extracted edge.

source_species_detail: Astrocytes and contusive SCI mice with bFGF injection, RhoA pathway analysis, YAP conditional deletion, and locomotor testing
citation_note: FGF2-RhoA-YAP astrocyte proliferation after SCI
evidence_summary: FGF2 was upregulated after SCI and activated a RhoA-YAP-p27 pathway that promoted astrocyte proliferation, glial-scar formation, and functional recovery in the tested model.
limitations: The study does not resolve FGFR1/2 or FRS2 adaptor identity; the extracted edge is functional/pathway evidence.

source_species_detail: EAE spinal cord, spinal neuron-microglia cocultures, inflammatory IL-1beta treatment, and WNT-ROR2 inhibition
citation_note: WNT5A-ROR2 noncanonical JNK and neuron-death branch
evidence_summary: Noncanonical WNT components including ROR2 increased in spinal neurons during EAE; WNT-ROR2 inhibition suppressed microglia-associated neuron death.
limitations: Pathway inhibition and disease expression support a functional branch but do not prove a direct WNT5A-ROR2 binding edge.

source_species_detail: Mouse spinal neural stem/progenitor cells treated with WNT5A and transplanted after SCI
citation_note: WNT5A-MAPK/JNK neural differentiation and SCI repair
evidence_summary: WNT5A increased pJNK and promoted neuronal differentiation through miRNA/RhoA regulation, improving histological and motor outcomes after transplantation into SCI mice.
limitations: Receptor complex is not resolved; this is a pathway/function edge.

source_species_detail: Reactive astrocytes and astrocyte-derived neural stem cells after cerebral ischemia; Notch1 cKO, GSI, promoter, and pSTAT3 assays
citation_note: Jagged1-Notch1-STAT3-ETBR astrocyte branch
evidence_summary: Jagged1/Notch1 signaling increased pSTAT3 and EDNRB/ETBR transcription and was required for reactive astrocyte proliferation in the tested brain-injury systems.
limitations: Brain ischemia rather than SCI; branch is retained as CNS comparator evidence.

source_species_detail: Rat SCI with Jagged1-positive or Jagged1-deficient endothelial progenitor cell transplantation and Delta-like-1 comparison
citation_note: Jagged1-Notch-Hes5 astrogliosis and recovery after SCI
evidence_summary: Jagged1-positive endothelial progenitors increased Hes5, acute astrogliosis, vascular effects, and functional recovery; Delta-like-1 substitution did not reproduce the same response.
limitations: The study supports pathway/function layers and ligand-context distinction but does not isolate every Notch paralog or downstream molecular step.

source_species_detail: Human NOTCH1-DLL1/DLL4 biochemical/reporter assays and mammalian ligand-strength comparisons
citation_note: NOTCH1 ligand-selective signal strength
evidence_summary: DLL4 bound and activated NOTCH1 more strongly than DLL1 in the cited human receptor assays; mammalian ligand comparisons show quantitative differences in HES1 signaling.
limitations: This is signaling-strength evidence associated with ligand/receptor constructs; it does not change Module 20A LR classifications.

source_species_detail: Adult rat lesioned CNS with glial-scar astrocytes and cultured hippocampal astrocytes
citation_note: CNTFR-alpha expression and functional CNTF receptor complex in astrocytes
evidence_summary: CNTFR-alpha expression shifted to astrocytes in the glial scar at the edge of a CNS lesion; cultured astrocytes contained a functional CNTF receptor complex capable of signal transduction.
limitations: The lesion model is CNS injury rather than a defined contusive SCI paradigm, and the study does not isolate CNTFR-alpha/gp130/LIFR from CNTFR-alpha/gp130/OSMR or provide receptor-proximal kinase perturbation in injured SCI astrocytes.

source_species_detail: Acute mouse SCI with spinal neurons and microglia/macrophages; FGF10 treatment and receptor/kinase assays
citation_note: FGF10-FGFR2-PI3K-AKT signaling after SCI
evidence_summary: FGF10 and FGFR2-associated PI3K-AKT signaling increased after acute SCI; FGF10 treatment improved neuronal survival and reduced injury-associated damage.
limitations: The study does not support an astrocyte receiver branch; exact FGFR2 adaptor ordering is not fully isolated.

source_species_detail: Mouse SCI with astrocytes, perivascular fibroblasts, macrophages/microglia, PDGFB/PDGFD localization, and SU16f treatment
citation_note: PDGFR-beta pathway and fibrotic scar after SCI
evidence_summary: PDGFB was mainly astrocyte-derived and PDGFD mainly macrophage/microglia- and fibroblast-derived; PDGFR-beta blockade reduced fibrotic scar and improved axon and locomotor outcomes.
limitations: The source supports pathway and functional output resolution; it does not establish a direct ligand-receptor binding edge or intracellular adaptor ordering.

source_species_detail: Mouse SCI spinal neural stem/progenitor cells with VEGF treatment and EGFR/VEGFR pathway inhibition
citation_note: VEGF-EGFR transactivation in spinal neural stem cells after SCI
evidence_summary: VEGF promoted spinal neural stem-cell activation through EGFR transactivation and increased proliferation/activation outputs after SCI.
limitations: VEGFR paralog identity and astrocyte receiver involvement are not resolved; do not promote to a direct VEGFR2 edge.

source_species_detail: Astrocyte-specific Ryk conditional-knockout mice and injured mouse/human spinal cord
citation_note: Astrocytic RYK and SCI wound healing
evidence_summary: RYK was induced at the injured spinal-cord scar border; astrocyte-specific Ryk deletion altered astrocyte morphology, differentiation, signaling, and wound healing.
limitations: Canonical WNT changes were measured; the proposed noncanonical PCP branch remains untested.

source_species_detail: Human reactive astrocytes, mouse EAE spinal-cord astrocytes, astrocyte-specific DLL4/NOTCH1 perturbations, NICD promoter, IL-6 blockade, and pSTAT3 assays
citation_note: DLL4-NOTCH1-IL6-STAT3 reactive astrocyte branch
evidence_summary: DLL4-NOTCH1 signaling increased IL-6 transcription through NICD promoter interaction and drove IL-6-dependent STAT3 phosphorylation and astrocyte reactivity.
limitations: The in vivo model is EAE/CNS neuroinflammation rather than contusive SCI; no Notch2/3/4 branch is established.

source_species_detail: Adult mouse contusive SCI and E18 rat primary cortical neurons with TNFR2 agonism and PI3K-gamma inhibitor comparison
citation_note: TNFR2-PI3Kgamma neuronal protection after contusive SCI
evidence_summary: TNFR2-specific agonism protected neurons and improved recovery after contusive SCI, while PI3K-gamma inhibition reduced the protective response.
limitations: The in vivo injury model and in vitro neuronal model use different species; the source supports a receptor-proximal pathway branch and perturbation dependence, not a direct physical TNFR2-PI3Kgamma interaction or astrocyte-specific mechanism.

source_species_detail: Focal mouse SCI with lesion-border astrocytes, perilesional microglia, astrocyte-targeted Csf1 deletion, and astrocyte-targeted Ifnar1 deletion
citation_note: CSF1 and IFN-beta astrocyte-microglia repair crosstalk after focal SCI
evidence_summary: Lesion-border astrocytes supplied CSF1 for microglial proliferation and repair, while microglial IFN-beta supported astrocyte survival; astrocyte-specific loss of either branch impaired wound repair and motor recovery.
limitations: The study establishes cell-source and functional pathway relationships but does not isolate direct CSF1-CSF1R binding, CSF1R kinase ordering, or every IFNAR-proximal kinase event.
